answer: Each identity registers a karst grove spring and locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files a mirror-gauge reading with a fresh serial and flow. A grove auditor recomputes discharge from karst conduit and rainfall tables; a reading outside 3 percent, reused serial, or shared spring burns the bond. First filing costs 36 credits; the kth fake pays 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6030 and 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-spring ring fails: each mirror gauge serial binds to one spring key. An honest keeper pays 36 once, reclaiming its bond after audit.
